strategies.name: Agent-society and wargame simulation forecasting for geopolitics ladders

strategies.name: Simulated stakeholder polling: synthetic electorates and twin panels
strategies.one_line: Build a trace- or interview-grounded synthetic population, poststratify it, and nowcast vote shares or poll and approval prints in thin or under-polled markets where no professional poll exists.
strategies.scope: Cover silicon sampling as a poll substitute in three forms. (a) PoSSUM-style social-trace agents with MrP for thin regional, foreign and primary election markets. (b) A standing interview-grounded twin panel re-polled daily for approval-rating and UMich sentiment brackets. (c) A weekly poll-print nowcast that supplies only the delta on a carry-forward baseline. State the negative evidence plainly: simulated respondents retrieve country-level and item-mean priors, LLMs explain 3.05% of respondent-specific variance, and the documented biases are progressive skew, third-party collapse and mode collapse. Explain why only real grounding data and a debiasing layer can help. Quantify capacity: print markets hold $50 to $10k, and liquid US races are already priced off professional aggregates. Include the hybrid tier where one commissioned real micro-poll calibrates or overrides the synthetic one, with value-of-information arithmetic and the Theo precedent. Give forward-only pre-registered validation. Boundary: simulations of small elite electorates are in elite-selection-bargaining-simulators.

Election contracts are restricted in several jurisdictions.

strategies.name: Named-member twins of small decision bodies (central banks, legislatures, courts) for second-order markets
strategies.one_line: Give each named voter one agent grounded in their speeches and votes. Simulate the vote conditional on the headline decision and trade the dissent-count, vote-split, wording and pivotal-member markets that have no institutional anchor.
strategies.scope: Cover per-member simulation of bodies with public individual records. For FOMC, ECB and BoE, cover dissent-count ladders, statement wording and presser word lists, conditional on the decision the futures already price. For legislatures, cover whip counts on the 5-10 pivotal members, with agenda timing modelled separately by a base-rate model. For courts, cover vote splits and opinion authorship after oral argument. Present the evidence honestly. FedSight's 93.75% has no futures baseline and no leakage control. Roll-call accuracy is mostly trivial party-line prediction. The classical SCOTUS model reaches 70.2%. Aaru could not simulate Powell. Address the under-prediction of dissent from 'farcical harmony', turnover, and statistical power: 8 meetings a year against the ~350-prediction bar, which forces pooling across bodies. Give the live liquidity gap of $8.07M on the decision vs $4.3k on dissents. Give forward-only validation and a mode-collapse kill check. Boundaries: secret-ballot electorates and coalition talks are in elite-selection-bargaining-simulators. UMA voter simulation is in synthetic-uma-dispute-jury.

strategies.name: Closed-electorate selection and coalition-bargaining simulators (structure first, role-play second)
strategies.one_line: Combine network and veto-player structure, a deterministic bargaining solver and agent straw polls. Use them to flag structurally dead longshots in selection markets and to price rule-aware coalition ladders.
strategies.scope: Cover secret or elite selection events: UN Secretary-General, Nobel committee, conclave, TIME Person of the Year. Also cover government-formation ladders. The thesis to examine is that structure worked where naive LLM elicitation failed: the Bocconi conclave network study ranked Prevost central while pundits and AI models missed him. Cover multiplex-network priors, successive straw polls with veto ballots, and coalition talks grounded in party manifestos and mapped through the market's exact rule, for example a party counts only if it holds a cabinet minister. Cover the Bueno-de-Mesquita-style hybrid where LLMs elicit only position, salience and clout and a transparent solver plays the dynamics. Tie selection to the favourite-longshot evidence: purchases below 10c lose 19.3c per dollar, but the sign flips when contracts are grouped by event. Give name-masked retro-tests and a forward test of a flagged-longshot short basket against an unselected one. Boundary: bodies whose members vote publicly are in decision-body-member-twins.

strategies.name: Critic-pool and awards-voter twins for mechanically aggregated scores
strategies.one_line: Treat the Tomatometer, or an awards ballot, as a sum of verdicts by an enumerable panel with public track records. Model each member, convolve into a bracket distribution before the embargo lifts, then Bayes-update on the early reviews.
strategies.scope: Cover a per-critic fresh/rotten propensity model: a statistical core plus an optional LLM persona built from each critic's review corpus. Cover roster and filing-time simulation against the resolution snapshot. Cover the Poisson-binomial bracket distribution, the selection bias in the first 20-40 reviews, and the post-embargo Beta-Binomial update. Extend to Oscars side categories using guild-bloc archetypes and preferential counting. State the evidence honestly. Synthetic panels do well on aggregates at 90% of test-retest. LLM taste simulation is 'super-omnivorous', so it predicts fresh too often. Individual twins correlate r=0.20 with their humans. Humans already trade Rotten Tomatoes scores statistically on Kalshi. Once ~30-50 reviews are in, the twin adds nothing. Capacity: Polymarket RT ladders hold $2.7k-$31.6k. Validate leak-free by backtesting the pure statistical model on 100 films first. Add the LLM layer only if it improves bracket log-loss at embargo plus 6 hours. Boundary: spoken-word twins are in speaker-twin-mention-montecarlo.

strategies.name: Speaker-twin Monte Carlo for mention markets (scripted speakers, maker expression)
strategies.one_line: Generate hundreds of synthetic transcripts per event and count strike-word hits under the exact resolution rules. Blend with base rates and the market price, and express the result only as skewed maker quotes.
strategies.scope: Cover the pipeline: a per-speaker, per-venue corpus; 200-500 simulated speeches or earnings calls, including Q&A from analyst twins; strict rule parsing for plurals, compounds and who counts as the speaker; a hierarchical Beta-Binomial base rate; and a market-prior blend. The evidence says the twin alone loses. On 856 Kalshi earnings-call contracts the LLM scored Brier 0.1470 against 0.1402 for the market, and the blend reached 0.1392. One public live system lost $16.40 over 1,115 bets. The documented profit came from a structural NO-side maker ladder (self-reported), not from LLM probabilities. Restrict use to templated speakers, because Trump-class improvisers are not simulable. Cover the cross-venue rule divergence, where Polymarket counts anyone on the broadcast and Kalshi only named speakers. Cover the live ASR leg, capacity of about $1k per word, and the taker fee of 0.04 x p(1-p) against zero for makers. Validate with 300+ word-contracts, forward-only, keeping separate arms for base rate only and for the blend.

strategies.name: Synthetic crowd with an internal market: LMSR wealth dynamics, wagering and meta-prediction
strategies.one_line: Have heterogeneous agents (different model families and different evidence shards) trade or wager internally so that money-weighted credibility self-calibrates. Add second-order questions that separate 'the market knows something' from 'the market is wrong'. Trade only the gated divergence from Polymarket.
strategies.scope: Cover three mechanism-design aggregators for an in-house agent crowd. (a) An internal LMSR whose agent bankrolls compound on resolved markets, which makes wealth updates a form of Bayesian model averaging. (b) WALLA-style incentive-compatible wagering, where aggregate stake sets position size. (c) Meta-prediction: each agent reports its own probability, its predicted peer mean and its predicted market price. This enables peer-prediction weighting, a surprisingly-popular correction and a 'knowledgeable dissent' filter. The file's centre is the monoculture constraint: rho = 0.70, ten agents behave like about 1.4 independent forecasters, a 10-agent market scored below a single agent, and persona prompts do not decorrelate. The file must state the obligation to beat a plain logistic aggregator or be dropped. Include N_eff health metrics and kill rules, cost, and a replay on 400+ post-cutoff markets with ablations. Boundaries: evidence-partition design is in information-partitioned-delphi-panel. Blending and gating against the price is in market-anchored-selective-deference. Conversational debate is in adversarial-debate-price-residual.

strategies.name: Multi-agent adversarial debate applied as a residual on the market price
strategies.one_line: Cross-family bull and bear advocates, plus a price-blind judge, produce a probability that is only ever applied as a logit-space correction to the Polymarket price. An independent-ensemble control arm can switch the debate off.
strategies.scope: Cover debate architectures for forecasting. Sides are assigned across model vendors. Every claim must cite evidence. The judge is blind to price and identity. The market mix is fitted per category. Sizing uses proper betting, not Kelly. Present the mixed evidence. Deliberation helped only for diverse model families: -0.020 log loss at p=0.017. Deliberative consensus scored about 76% against 83.43% for independent aggregation. Conformity and sycophancy are common, persuasion can override truth, and token cost is 2.1-3.4x. Cover two variants. In the veto-only variant a red-team agent never generates trades and only halves or vetoes candidates from a statistical signal, for example recalibrating political favourites; the recalibration alpha itself belongs to the behavioural-bias band. In the rationale-quality variant the judge weights agents by Explanation Quality Markers and a Martingale entrenchment score. Include existing Polymarket attempts such as PolySwarm, none of which reports PnL. Validate with a Hindcast-style four-arm backtest on 400+ markets, then 350 forward forecasts. Boundary: market mechanisms between agents are in internal-agent-prediction-market.

strategies.name: Information-partitioned Delphi panel (designed evidence asymmetry)
strategies.one_line: Give each agent a disjoint private slice of the evidence plus a shared public core, and allow only rationale exchange. Diversity then comes from information, not persona adjectives. Use the output as a filter and sizing input.
strategies.scope: Cover the InfoDelphi design. Documents are routed by BM25 relevance into a public core and private shards. Partitions may be stakeholder or source lenses: legal filings, trade press, local press, on-chain flow. There are one or two rationale rounds. Aggregation is logit-space with confidence weights. Partitioning is kept orthogonal to model family. The key result is a Brier improvement from 0.216 to 0.178 on 375 Polymarket-derived questions. The gain vanishes when all evidence is shared, and the design was never benchmarked against the market price. Present the counter-evidence: debate can re-herd, and learned aggregation still loses to the market on clean questions. Conclude that this is a disagreement and uncertainty signal for other strategies, not standalone alpha. Include the OSINT sensor-swarm variant, where one agent per physical or bureaucratic feed holds private context. Validate by replication with a rho=1.0 ablation and an 8-week forward shadow run. Boundary: the language or allegiance silo whose signal is the difference between silos is in cross-lingual-source-silo-tilt.

strategies.name: Cross-lingual source-silo tilt on non-Anglophone and geopolitics markets
strategies.one_line: Hold the model fixed and forecast twice, once from English-only context and once from local-language primary sources. Apply the difference as a tilt to the market price, mainly in fee-free geopolitics markets.
strategies.scope: Cover agents restricted to one information ecosystem each: English wire, local official and military-analytical sources, adversary media, OSINT. Cover per-silo bias calibration on resolved markets. Define the signal as local minus English, not either forecast alone. Add the latency leg on local primary publications. The anchor result is that English news context was wrong 64-72% of the time on Ukraine territorial-capture pushes across four models, that the bias lives in the sources, and that Ukrainian sources reduce it. The file must state the gap: the paper uses the market as its reference, so nobody has shown that Polymarket PRICES share the bias. Cover the fact that arbiter maps and media, not ground truth, settle these markets (the ISW edit). Cover local-source propaganda, local traders already being present, insider flow, and single-theatre overfit. Validate with a Hindcast-style replay on 300+ non-Anglosphere markets that tests price plus lambda times tilt. Boundary: generic evidence partitioning is in information-partitioned-delphi-panel.

strategies.name: Market-anchored stacking and selective deference (edge map, abstention gates, day-zero quoting)
strategies.one_line: Treat the question 'should we disagree with the price here?' as the prediction problem. Make the market mid an expert in an online stacker and route by lifecycle and price cell. Monetise the residual as maker skew, especially in the first hours of new and toss-up markets.
strategies.scope: Cover the fail-safe blend layer. Use Hedge or BOA online aggregation with the price in the expert pool, so the weight on agents falls to zero when they carry no information. Keep per-cell weights with a published prior of about 0.33 AI and 0.67 market. Build a hierarchical-Bayes sleeping-experts edge map over category, lifecycle stage, price band and liquidity, net of the fee formula. Add Thompson-sampling routing, abstention, and conformal or unanimity act-abstain gates. Cover the opening-quote business: detect listings, take the prior from the panel, sibling-market bounds and other venues, quote wide and two-sided, then taper as volume arrives. Key numbers: Brier skill vs the market of +0.167 at open+1 against -0.829 at close-1, and +0.301 on toss-ups. No two-model ensemble beats the market overall. The blend gains about 0.005 Brier. Purchases at 90c or above earn 0.83c per dollar. Give the fee arithmetic, the adverse selection faced by new-market quoters, event-clustered validation on 400+ markets, and markout tests. Boundary: how the agents are produced is in the other forecasting files.

strategies.name: Recursive self-improving forecaster: outcome-RL on market-relative profit plus governed experience memory
strategies.one_line: A single forecaster improves itself from its own resolved-market log. It is fine-tuned weekly with RLVR, rewarded by fee-adjusted proper-betting payoff against the logged price, and it keeps a curated and decaying lesson memory. It is deployed only in high-repetition market families and only as one expert in the stacker.
strategies.scope: Cover the two self-improvement loops that act on one agent. (1) Continual outcome-RL on a 7-32B open model. Build the training asset: question, rules, frozen news snapshot, executable bid/ask and outcome. Make the reward market-relative proper-betting profit, not raw Brier. Use state-conditioned empirical-frequency rewards for fast templated families. Enforce a time-truncation harness. Use median sampling at inference. Counter forgetting under weekly updates. (2) Verbal RL: post-mortem lessons held in an Experience Bank and a Meta-Guideline Bank, each with utility weights, decay and retirement, routed through a per-family harness tree. Present the promising results: a 14B model matching o1 with >10% simulated ROI, and Live-Evo's +20.8% Brier. Present the three negative 2026 results: dense updates peak and then decline, memory fails on low-repetition streams, and curation decides whether experience helps or hurts. Discuss label-rate limits and GPU cost for a small team. Validate with a memory on/off A/B across templated families and the weight earned in the stacker. Boundary: population-level evolution is in evolutionary-agent-strategy-factory.

strategies.name: Evolutionary agent population and autoresearch strategy factory
strategies.one_line: Evolve a quality-diversity archive of agents whose fitness is marginal contribution to the market-anchored blend. Run a leakage-guarded autoresearch loop that proposes structural strategies. Breed new agents by recombining modules that carry positive PnL attribution.
strategies.scope: Cover population-level self-improvement. A MAP-Elites archive over model family, information diet and niche, with Numerai-MMC-style leave-one-out fitness, so that selection buys orthogonality and not another copy of the consensus. GEPA-style reflective prompt mutation. A keep-or-revert autoresearch loop over the full trade archive, restricted to point-in-time tool registries, with thresholds deflated by trial count and an untouched event-clustered holdout. Compositional breeding of typed modules (signal, sizing, execution) using an attribution ledger. An ecological co-evolution gym that replays the team's own L2 books against reactive rival archetypes, including fee and tick perturbations taken from the changelog. Include the hard negatives: honest evaluation rejected every LLM-discovered equity strategy, a leaky Sharpe-35 oracle passed DSR and PBO, 70% of mutations were reverted, and greedy search is a strong default. Include the hobby systems elastifund and atlas-gic, and the builder-fee commercial layer. Validation: planted-edge recovery, sim-to-live rank agreement, top-k chosen by marginal contribution vs top-k chosen by own Brier. Boundary: promotion statistics are in evaluation-promotion-allocation-metalayer.

strategies.name: Meta-layer: leak-free evaluation, anytime-valid promotion, label-free fitness, capital allocation and changelog-reactive re-optimisation
strategies.one_line: Build the selection-risk machinery every speculative agent needs. Cutoff-staggered time-machine backtests. E-process promotion gates under online FDR control. Consistency-arbitrage as instant fitness. Bandit or internal-futarchy capital allocation. A watcher that re-tunes the whole book within hours of a Polymarket rule change.
strategies.scope: Cover five components. (1) A vintage panel with frozen web snapshots as the only trustworthy backtest. Contamination collapsed a 35.8% model gap to 8.9%, and prompted ignorance fails. Include the speculative news-value-gap signal. (2) Test-martingale promotion from replay to paper to $1-5 live to scaled. Bet at event-cluster level, because gates fired falsely 135 of 135 times on dependent streams. (3) The arbitrage-consistency violation score as a label-free inner-loop fitness, which correlates with Brier. Guard against the Goodhart drift toward 0.5. (4) Capital allocation across strategy bots using non-stationary Thompson sampling against an internal decision market. Expect the bandit to win. (5) Changelog-reactive re-optimisation. Diff the docs and fee tables, patch the simulator, re-backtest, reallocate. Use the six verified 2026 rule changes for a retro event study of competitor adaptation lag. State that none of this is alpha by itself. It prevents paying for fake alpha. Give simulation-based validation with synthetic edges of 0, 0.01, 0.02 and 0.04.

strategies.name: LLM-monoculture factor: model the bot herd, then front-run or fade it
strategies.one_line: Run a deliberately vanilla 'sentinel' consensus of default frontier-model bots to sense where homogeneous LLM traders lean. Learn its bias surface and its post-listing price impact. Provide liquidity against news-free drift toward it.
strategies.scope: Cover the Vanilla Consensus Index or shadow herd: 3-5 default-prompt frontier models with generic search. Cover the bias map built from resolved markets: acquiescence (YES bias), English-news bias, escalation bias, overconfidence. Cover the on-chain footprint tests: drift toward the sentinel without news, a 15-45 minute action cadence, synchronized small takers. Cover the two trades, quoting ahead of predicted flow and fading herd pushes with time stops. Cover the zero-capital use as a no-edge and crowding detector for the team's own agents. Evidence on homogeneity: rho 0.70, identical top picks in 92% of World Cup matches. Evidence on losses: Prediction Arena -16% to -31% on Kalshi, PolyBench 5 of 7 models losing. The decisive unknown: the LLM share of Polymarket volume is unmeasured. The '30% of wallets' figure is a vendor claim. Naively fading LLMs is also unprofitable. Include reflexivity and the need to re-learn after each model release. Validate by pure logging over 12 weeks: regress next-period returns on sentinel-minus-price, and track markouts from herd-matched wallets. Boundary: human trader-cohort simulation is in crowd-price-path-simulation.

strategies.name: Trade the crowd, not the outcome: trader-population simulation and price-path forecasting
strategies.one_line: Model who trades a market and how they under- or over-react. Use wallet-calibrated archetypes, LLM cohort reads of news, or a supervised belief-dynamics model. Trade the expected drift or reversal over hours to days, flat on the outcome.
strategies.scope: Cover price-path strategies with a fast-label feedback loop. A wallet-archetype agent-based replica of the order book: longshot buyers, momentum chasers, makers. Its behavioural core should be fitted statistically, because prompt personas fail. An LLM cohort debate on scheduled catalysts. Social-World-Model supervised baselines. A proxy-resolved p_7d target, in the manner of Numinous scoring. Under-reaction drift against a computable benchmark, where price adjusts 0.64-for-one. Fading dislocations of 5 points or more in low-prominence markets. Evidence that crowd bias is persistent and identifiable: sub-10c purchases lose 19.3c per dollar, the top decile of longshot buyers makes 26.6% of next month's low-price purchases, and 8 of 14 wallet parameters are stable. Evidence on persistence: field-experiment price shocks were still visible after 60 days. Strong negatives: StakeBench shows no LLM beats naive odds projection, only ~10% of Polymarket moves are attributable to news, feed-inferred trade direction is 59% accurate so on-chain fills are required, and fees bite on round trips. Staged validation: event study first, then a supervised baseline, and the simulator only if it adds accuracy.

strategies.name: Ex-ante rules layer: rule-lawyer scanner, ambiguity wargame, dispute-hazard haircut and rule-diff versioning
strategies.one_line: Compile every market's rules into a typed resolution spec. Have adversarial agents enumerate scenarios where headline truth and contract outcome diverge. Price the dispute and flip hazard like a credit spread, and archive rule diffs and clarifications. All of this happens before any dispute exists.
strategies.scope: Cover everything that reads rules text before resolution. (a) The spec compiler and the two-pass gap between a headline reader and a rules-aware reader, trading only divergences that have a named scenario. (b) A role-played panel: literalist proposer, spirit-of-the-market disputer, precedent-grounded voter. It produces a basis-risk score and a playbook. (c) A tabular hazard model of P(dispute), P(flip | dispute) and lock-up time, used to haircut 95-99c sniping and widen quotes. About 1% of proposals are disputed. 23.9% of disputed contracts revise. In markets above $6.8M, flagged questions are disputed 16.2% of the time against 8.1%. (d) Semantic versioning of rule text and on-chain 'Additional context' posts. (e) Cross-venue spec-diff for rule-basis pricing; equivalent markets sit 2-4% apart. The key limit: LLMs cannot predict disputes from rule text alone (accuracy 0.40-0.57), so use LLM-extracted features inside a tabular model. Validate with Du's 2,221 disputed contracts plus matched controls, and with a time-split AUC. Boundary: trading after a dispute opens is in synthetic-uma-dispute-jury.

strategies.name: Synthetic UMA jury: in-dispute adjudication trading with a unanimity gate
strategies.one_line: When a proposal is disputed, several web-enabled model families independently predict how UMA voters will rule. Trade only the unanimous high-confidence subset, where the price still carries a panic or lock-up discount.
strategies.scope: Cover the post-dispute window only. Subscribe to oracle lifecycle events; Data API v2 now exposes resolution lifecycle reads. Assemble the dossier: rules, clarifications, UMA evidence threads, dated news. Collect independent votes with no debate, since debate lowers accuracy. Gate on unanimity plus confidence. Size by lock-up time: 24-48h of debate plus ~48h of voting, longer with resets. Core numbers: LLMs agree with the final UMA ruling 89.58% of the time against a naive 'proposal stands' baseline of about 76%. The unanimous subset is 97.87% accurate on 47% of questions. Inter-model error correlation is 0.53-0.69. The key unknown is that nobody has measured price levels during dispute windows. Humans already specialise here; one wallet cluster won 26 of 34 contested markets. Discuss token-weighted whale voting, the fat-tailed ~10% misses, leakage in backtests of famous disputes, and oracle-surface changes. Validate by replaying 2026 disputes that fall after model cutoffs. Boundary: ex-ante hazard and rules reading are in rules-ambiguity-hazard-layer.

strategies.name: LLM- and simulation-derived dependence pricing: Polymarket Combos RFQ and cross-event joint distributions
strategies.one_line: Estimate cross-event dependence from precomputed conditional debates or coherent world simulations. Keep the market's marginals. Quote or pick off 2-50-leg Combo RFQs, and trade listed combos against their legs where joint probability differs from the independence product.
strategies.scope: Cover the dependence-only thesis. Simulation levels are biased, but dependence estimates partly cancel those biases, and hedged packages of combo against legs isolate the correlation view. Methods: offline pairwise conditional debates that produce log-odds ratios, a pairwise exponential-family or copula pricer fast enough for the 400 ms quote window, and 1,000+ world runs for linked clusters with a cheap first version that uses direct conditional elicitation. Cover the Combos mechanics from the docs: 2-50 YES legs, 10 s acceptance, last look needing about $2,500 of notional plus contact with Polymarket, a pause above 15% rejections, and 15 request creates per minute. Cover quoter mode and requester mode. The Kalshi evidence is that parlays are overpriced by about 3% per leg, and Kalshi mints 1.09M combinatorial objects a day. Limits: there is no ground truth for conditionals, relation accuracy is 62.8%, adverse selection, generative exaggeration that overstates correlations, capital lock-up, and sports desks that already price same-game correlation. Validate with an RFQ logging phase and 50 resolved linked pairs scored against independence. Boundary: logical-constraint coherence is in semantic-market-graph-relative-value.

strategies.name: Semantic market graph: coherent fair value, LLM-filtered lead-lag and precomputed catalyst playbooks
strategies.one_line: Build an adversarially verified graph of logical and causal links between live markets. Project prices onto the coherent polytope to get soft relative-value signals. Trade followers when semantically justified leaders move, and pre-write conditional orders for second-order markets before scheduled catalysts.
strategies.scope: Cover three uses of one graph. (1) Typed constraints: implication, exclusion, date nesting, threshold ladders. A red team tests each against the literal rules. An LP/IP projection yields soft residuals, and a debate decides which leg is wrong. Be frank that hard combinatorial arbitrage is tiny: about $95k realised against $39.5M of rebalancing, and 13 valid pairs out of 1,576 flagged. (2) Granger and temporal-graph leader-follower pairs, kept only if an LLM can justify a transmission mechanism. On Kalshi this raised the win rate from 51.4% to 54.5% and roughly halved the average loss. A separate backtest returned a 14.12% net ROI, but 76% of the PnL came from five trades. (3) Debate-built conditional playbooks that fire into stale second-order books after a catalyst. Precomputing removes the LLM's latency handicap. The defensive twin is catalyst-aware quote pulling. Cover fee drag at mid prices, rule-mismatch false edges, the tendency of LLMs to rationalise any pair, and capacity. Validate with edge-precision audits, residual IC, a lag event study and a walk-forward test. Boundary: joint-probability pricing is in dependence-pricing-combos-joint.

strategies.name: External forecaster sourcing: meta-aggregate public AI-forecast exhaust, mine Numinous SN6, run a staked tournament
strategies.one_line: Buy or borrow the thing an in-house LLM pool cannot produce, which is independently built forecasters. Learn an aggregator over public benchmark forecasts. Optionally earn emissions as a miner scored against the Polymarket price. Later run a Numerai-style commit-reveal tournament scored by marginal contribution.
strategies.scope: Cover three tiers of outside signal. (1) Ingest the Prophet Arena, Numinous and Metaculus-bot per-event forecasts. Map the events to Polymarket. Fit a regularised logistic aggregator with disagreement features, then blend it with the market and gate it. (2) Run an agent as a Bittensor SN6 miner. It is scored as S = (pred-target)^2 - (price-target)^2 against the 7-day-later Polymarket price. The rules require 85% coverage and a 240 s runtime, and roughly the top 20 earn. (3) A commit-reveal tournament on thin early-life markets, prize-only at first. Contributors are scored by MMC-style contribution to the blend, so copying the price earns nothing. The thesis: monoculture caps in-house diversity, and independently engineered systems decorrelate. Limits: top Prophet Arena agents only tie the Kalshi baseline. Public signals are contestable. Adverse selection means anyone with real edge trades it directly. Timestamps go stale. Emissions are paid in a volatile token. The 7-day target rewards predicting the crowd. Validate with an 8-week ingestion sprint (alpha CI at n of 350 or more) and a pilot that measures the stacker weight earned and rho against the in-house pool.

strategies.name: Sponsor-and-inform: subsidise depth in niches where simple statistical models beat the market, then be the informed maker
strategies.one_line: Find market families where a computed baseline demonstrably beats Polymarket prices, such as disease counts or thresholds with an options-implied reference. Pitch a market or pick a thin existing one. Pay for liquidity rewards so a book forms, and quote the bracket ladder from the model.
strategies.scope: Cover the inversion of the usual constraint, which is edge without depth. Domain discovery runs through a reference-class and base-rate pipeline: reference classes with computed base rates, not remembered ones; a red-team challenge on class membership; and a Fermi cross-check. Evidence for such niches: FluSight and simple baselines dominate Polymarket and Kalshi flu and measles markets, to the point that the optimal blend puts zero weight on the markets, and those markets price impossible outcomes. BTC threshold contracts sit 5.6 points from option-implied values. Counter-evidence: prompt-only 'superforecaster' tricks do almost nothing, and more capable models make worse tail forecasts. Mechanics: users cannot create markets and must suggest them via X. Anyone can sponsor rewards from $0.1 a day, with one sponsorship per market. In the Telonex case about $70k of sponsorship doubled the number of makers and multiplied top-of-book depth 23.5x. Economics to test: reward farmers dilute the subsidy, other makers copy your quotes, and adverse selection applies. The account is mark-out plus recaptured rewards plus rebates against sponsorship spend. Validate with 8 weeks of public model scoring, then a 14-day sponsorship at $20 a day.
sub_variants: Existing thin market with a dominant public baseline (measles, flu brackets)
Pitching a new market with a legible resolution source
Options-implied density vs BTC threshold ladders
Reference-class tournament with a Fermi cross-check as the model source
merged_from: Sponsor-and-inform: get a market listed where your model beats the crowd, buy its depth, then be the informed maker
Reference-class tournament with data-backed Fermi decomposition for structured markets
strategies.flags: Whether the ToS conduct code allows trading a market you lobbied for and sponsored is unverified. Check the wash and self-trade rules. Never misstate anything when pitching a market. Avoid death and disaster markets for reputational reasons. CDC backfills can break bracket settlement.

key_evidence.note: The FluSight ensemble dominates Polymarket and Kalshi disease markets. The optimal blend puts zero weight on the markets.
Anyone can sponsor rewards from $0.1 a day. One sponsorship per market. Refund from the next 00:00 UTC.
Users cannot create markets. They suggest a title, resolution source and demand evidence via X.
~$70k of sponsorship: makers 302 to 639, top-of-book depth 23.5x, all within a day.
Measles 2026: $7.98M volume but only $20.1k resting liquidity across 16 brackets.
Polymarket BTC thresholds sit a mean 5.6 points from option-implied values (t=6.46). Half-life ~4h. May be a premium rather than a mispricing.
38 forecasting prompts give negligible gains. Bayesian-reasoning prompts hurt. The edge must come from data pipelines.
What gets listed is driven by settlement legibility, not importance.

notes:
This band consolidates 6 lenses and about 80 candidates into 22 entries. I made no web calls in this consolidation step. Whether two candidates were duplicates was settled from the candidate texts and the evidence they share. Every URL is copied from the discovery input. Several lenses marked some URLs as 'listing only' or 'headline only', so file authors must re-fetch before relying on the numbers.

Seed coverage:
- agent-society simulation: agent-society-simulation-forecasting, plus crowd-price-path-simulation and dependence-pricing-combos-joint as society-sim derivatives.
- synthetic crowd / internal prediction market: internal-agent-prediction-market, plus information-partitioned-delphi-panel and external-forecaster-sourcing.
- adversarial debate: adversarial-debate-price-residual. The debate-over-legs variant sits inside semantic-market-graph-relative-value.
- self-improving / recursive: recursive-self-improving-forecaster, evolutionary-agent-strategy-factory, evaluation-promotion-allocation-metalayer, market-anchored-selective-deference.
- simulated stakeholder polling: simulated-stakeholder-polling, plus decision-body-member-twins, elite-selection-bargaining-simulators and synthetic-uma-dispute-jury.

Findings that recur across lenses and that every file should restate:
1. LLM panels lose to liquid prices standalone but add information as a ~0.33-weight blend. Skill sits early in a market's life and on toss-ups.
2. Monoculture is the binding constraint: rho ~0.7, and ten agents behave like ~1.4 independent forecasters. Only model-family diversity and evidence diversity decorrelate agents. Persona prompts do not.
3. Deliberation often hurts, so always run an independent-aggregation control arm.
4. Backtests inside a model's training window are void. Validate forward-only or with frozen snapshots.
5. Detecting a 0.02 edge takes ~350 independent resolved predictions. Count clustered events as one.
6. Fee arithmetic (taker fee = feeRate x p(1-p), makers pay 0, Geopolitics is fee-free) pushes almost every idea toward maker expression or the fee-free category.
7. Most markets where simulation has a structural argument are tiny: side markets hold $50 to tens of thousands of dollars. The liquid exceptions are Nobel, UNSG, TIME POTY, geopolitics ladders and non-English elections.

Build order the lenses suggest: evaluation-promotion-allocation-metalayer and market-anchored-selective-deference are infrastructure for everything else. rules-ambiguity-hazard-layer and synthetic-uma-dispute-jury fit the owner's existing sniping stack best and are text-only with on-chain ground truth. llm-monoculture-herd-factor, crowd-price-path-simulation and dependence-pricing-combos-joint are the most novel and have the weakest support.

Three entries bundle several strategies and will need sub-sectioned files: rules-ambiguity-hazard-layer, semantic-market-graph-relative-value and evaluation-promotion-allocation-metalayer. If the owner prefers more files to fewer, the natural splits are rule-diff versioning, catalyst playbooks and changelog-reactive re-optimisation.
